summary: Extending the existing client-probe.mjs is an appropriate smallest increment and fits user authorization. The check mapping to AC-2/AC-4/AC-7 is sound, and the runtime/network/data/persistence/mutation holds are clear. The plan omits AC-7 in its own acceptance section, does not bind the exact owned files and executable verification path, and does not clearly separate future actual-runtime research from this synthetic-only increment. The local lockfile and installed @opencode/sdk@2.0.18 manifest do not prove current fresh registry availability; the npm default version being reserved is not inconsistent with a cached local version.

open_findings.finding: Add AC-7 to plan acceptance criteria and explicitly bind the sdk-client-probe check to AC-2/AC-4/AC-7 without implying actual runtime or full product completion.

Specify exact owned files, TypeScript config inclusion, verify.mjs wiring, unchanged package/lock/dependency versions, and that the command fails on any TS or runtime-case failure. Existing host/UI checks are regressions only, not runtime proof. If cache is missing, do not install or access network.

Mark actual runtime/service/event/network probe as a future candidate requiring its own plan and review, with package availability, isolation and lifecycle effects unresolved. This increment grants no host start/discovery/network/file access/write/persistence authority.
